item.title: Anuel AA Opens Up About Quitting Drinking & Smoking
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Anuel AA says he stopped drinking and smoking about six months ago as he prepares Real Hasta la Muerte 2 for November 19.
item.content:encoded:
Anuel AA says he stopped drinking and smoking about six months ago, describing a change in his daily life as he prepares to release his first album in four years.

The Puerto Rican rapper discussed his habits with Leila Cobo in a Billboard interview filmed on a yacht in Miami. He linked the decision to growing older and learning from his experiences.

“I don’t smoke anymore,” he said. Asked when his lifestyle began to change, he added: “It started about six months ago.”

He said he feels more alert now. His days include eating well and working on music and business.

“Drugs don’t fulfill you, fame doesn’t fulfill you, money doesn’t fulfill you,” Anuel said.

The update comes as he nears a return he’s been building toward for months. His last album, LLNM2, arrived in 2022. The next project brings him back to the name of his 2018 debut while leaving room for the Mexican music that has taken over much of his listening.

At Billboard Latin Music Week in October, Anuel laid out plans for two albums. One would carry trap and reggaeton.

The other would focus on corridos, a style he spent much of the year hearing while traveling through Mexico. He described that project as a gift to the country.

He had already worked within that scene. In July, Anuel joined Luis R Conriquez and Fuerza Regida on “Hay Con Que” from Conriquez’s Muchacho Alegre. His interest in corridos put him alongside artists he regarded as friends and whose records he also played as a fan.

He had also tied the long break between albums to spending more time with his children and family. He continued releasing music during that stretch, including “Vuelve,” which came out October 9 as he worked toward both planned projects.

In the interview, Anuel said Real Hasta la Muerte 2 will arrive November 19. He is still finishing Cartel Real Hasta la Muerte and may release it that day, too. Working with Mexican musicians has meant learning a different way to sing. He said Fuerza Regida would produce songs for the project.

item.title: Anderson .Paak And Cordae Claim First Billboard Rap Albums No. 1
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Anderson .Paak and Cordae earn their first Billboard Top Rap Albums No. 1 as Heavy Is The Crown opens with 30,000 units.
item.content:encoded:
Anderson .Paak and Cordae have turned their first full album together into a career first for both artists.

Heavy Is The Crown debuted at No. 1 on Billboard’s Top Rap Albums chart. The project earned 30,000 equivalent album units in the United States during the tracking week ending October 29.

The result gives .Paak and Cordae their first chart-topper on Top Rap Albums. Heavy Is The Crown also entered Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums at No. 2 and opened at No. 11 on the Billboard 200.

The Top Rap Albums chart blends traditional album sales with streaming-equivalent and track-equivalent units. That mix gave the duo a broad measure of how the project moved during its first full week in the market.

Those numbers sharpen the picture that emerged when the album first arrived. AllHipHop previously reported that the project reached No. 10 on the HITS Top 50 with an estimated 30,290 units. Billboard’s final chart uses Luminate data and places the album at No. 11 on the Billboard 200 with 30,000 units.

The 11-track album was released October 23 through APE####, Mass Appeal Records and EMPIRE. “Airbender” led the set in streaming activity with 2.4 million official on-demand streams in the United States during the opening frame.

Heavy Is The Crown arrived while Cordae faced a contract lawsuit from his former label, which sought to challenge his right to release new music. The album still reached listeners on schedule and now gives both collaborators a new chart milestone.

.Paak has spent years moving between rap, soul and R&B, both as a solo artist and as one half of Silk Sonic. Cordae built his reputation on tightly written solo albums and collaborations before joining .Paak for a full project.

Their shared record pushed each of them beyond earlier Top Rap Albums peaks.

The pairing also widened the album’s reach. .Paak brought a live-band feel and an easy vocal range. Cordae supplied compact verses and a direct rap center. The chart results show that the combination reached buyers and streamers at the same time.

The No. 1 debut also gives the album a clear identity beyond its first-week sales estimate. Heavy Is The Crown now stands as the top rap album on the chart dated November 7, with two artists collecting their first crown on the same release.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Kiotti Brown Keeps On The Radar Trademark Fight In Houston
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Kiotti Brown kept his On The Radar trademark suit in Houston after a judge cited the company's recording sessions with 75 artists.
item.content:encoded:
Kiotti Brown kept his trademark fight with On The Radar Productions LLC in Houston after a federal judge rejected the New York company’s request to dismiss the case on venue.

Judge Andrew S. Hanen ruled that the company’s Houston recording stop gave the court authority to hear Brown’s claims. The order also rejected its argument that Houston was the wrong venue.

The Houston rapper and media personality, also known as “Radio Boss,” accused the company of infringing his “On tha Radar” trademark. His lawsuit alleges that the competing name confused audiences, cost him listeners and customers and hurt his revenue and reputation.

Brown alleged that he began using “ON THE RADAR” and “ON THA RADAR” in 2016 for radio, podcasts, video programming and live entertainment.

He applied to register “ON THA RADAR” in June 2021 and received the federal registration on October 31, 2023. On The Radar claimed it began using its name in 2018.

The company traveled to Houston in December 2023 for a recording run that became central to Judge Hanen’s decision.

“To produce this content, OTR spent four days recording content with 75 artists at a Houston establishment known as The Closet,” Judge Hanen wrote.

Its crew used an “ON THE RADAR” neon sign and promoted the resulting series as a Houston edition. The sessions produced 75 long-form YouTube videos and 76 YouTube Shorts, according to the order. Brown asserted that at least 35 of the featured artists were based in Houston.

The name dispute escalated when On The Radar asked the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board to cancel Brown’s registration on August 1, 2025. Brown answered that petition the following month and filed this federal lawsuit on May 14, 2026.

On The Radar argued that it had no Texas office, property or employees. It also pointed to the absence of contracts with the artists or The Closet, merchandise sales and local sponsors. The company maintained that any relevant infringement occurred when it published the material in New York.

Judge Hanen focused on the work the company did inside Houston and its use of the disputed name there.

“It is sufficient to acknowledge that Plaintiff is alleging harm as a result of OTR’s use of the mark in its activities and that these activities occurred in Houston and directly targeted at the city of Houston, regardless of whether it was later published to a globally-accessible internet market,” Judge Hanen wrote.

The company contended that both sides had used their names peacefully until 2025 without confusion. Brown alleged that their overlapping use in Houston damaged his business. Judge Hanen found enough connection between the Houston sessions and Brown’s claims for the suit to proceed there.

“Thus, Plaintiff’s claim for trademark infringement at the very least relates to OTR’s use of the mark as it did in Texas,” the order stated.

On The Radar also argued that its witnesses and discovery materials were in New York. Judge Hanen weighed that burden against Brown’s interest in suing where the alleged business harm occurred.

“While it may be a burden on OTR to litigate this claim in Texas rather than in its home state of New York, that burden does not outweigh the other factors, all of which favor allowing Plaintiff’s claim to proceed in Texas,” Judge Hanen wrote.

The same Houston stop supported keeping the case in the Southern District of Texas.

“For the foregoing reasons, venue is appropriate as OTR’s Houston-leg of the multi-city tour at least in part gave rise to the claim at issue,” Judge Hanen concluded.

item.title: Omari Hardwick Breaks Silence On Power Fallout
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Omari Hardwick addresses the shift behind Power while keeping his support for 50 Cent and Courtney Kemp intact.
item.content:encoded:
Omari Hardwick is finally talking about the tension behind his exit from Power, while still supporting both 50 Cent and Courtney Kemp.

The actor addressed the long-running dispute during an Associated Press interview tied to his role in the Prime Video series The Greatest.

Asked whether he knew Kemp wanted his character, James “Ghost” St. Patrick, removed earlier than the show’s sixth and final season, Hardwick said, “There was definitely a shift.”

Hardwick did not name a single person as the cause. He framed the problem as something gifted people can face even when a project is successful. He also made it clear that years of public debate didn’t push him to choose one side.

“I never said anything, did I?” Hardwick asked. He added, “I always rock with 50. I always pray for Courtney.”

That answer arrives as 50 Cent and Kemp continue to challenge each other’s version of how Power came together and who shaped its biggest decisions.

50 has said he fought to keep Ghost alive after Kemp wanted the character gone. Kemp has disputed his account while acknowledging his part in bringing the crime drama to television. The argument has kept the show’s leadership decisions in public view years later.

Hardwick’s relationship with the franchise has also been strained.

He previously said his pay did not match the weight of leading one of Starz’s signature shows. 50 later said the actor placed too much value on himself, adding another layer to a partnership that helped turn Ghost into a television fixture.

The latest comments set a clear boundary. Hardwick confirmed that the working climate changed and kept his answer focused on the people he still supports.

His next chapter is already moving.

AllHipHop previously reported that Hardwick’s Bosch prequel is set to premiere in January. In The Greatest, he plays a younger version of Muhammad Ali’s father, Cassius Clay Sr., in a story built around the family that shaped the boxing legend.

For Power fans, the interview offers the clearest answer Hardwick has given about the split. He saw the shift and kept quiet. Even now, he is leaving room for both 50 Cent and Kemp in the story.

item.title: Master P’s Son Hercy Miller Will Play Him In Snoop Dogg Biopic
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Hercy Miller will make his feature-film debut as his father, Master P, in Universal's Snoop Dogg biopic, now in production.
item.content:encoded:
Hercy Miller will make his feature-film debut by playing his father, Master P, in Universal’s Snoop Dogg biopic.

Deadline first reported the casting as the movie added three more people to its expanding ensemble. Zachariah Rogers will portray The D.O.C., while actor and comedian Tyquan Givens, also known as Watts Homie Quan, will play an original character named B. Mack.

Miller’s role gives the film a direct family link to one of the most important turns in Snoop Dogg’s career. Master P signed Snoop to No Limit Records in 1998 after the rapper left Death Row Records.

Snoop released Da Game Is to Be Sold, Not to Be Told that year, beginning a three-album run with the New Orleans label.

That chapter also connected two very different independent empires. Master P had built No Limit through a high-volume release schedule and distribution deal with Priority Records. Snoop entered the company as an established star looking for a new business home.

The younger Miller has spent much of his public life in basketball. He played college ball at Tennessee State, Louisville and Southern Utah before appearing on the Netflix reality series “Calabasas Confidential.” The Master P role now moves him into a scripted feature centered on his own family’s history.

“Snoop” is currently in production and is scheduled to reach theaters on August 6, 2027. Jonathan Daviss stars as Snoop Dogg, with Craig Brewer directing from his rewrite of Joe Robert Cole’s original script.

The cast already includes Myles Bullock Be as Dr. Dre, Camron Jones as Tupac Shakur, Algee Smith as Warren G, Tre Hale as Suge Knight and SwayvoTwain as The Notorious B.I.G. Lauren London plays Snoop’s mother, Beverly Tate, and Laya DeLeon Hayes plays Shante Taylor.

Cynthia Erivo recently joined the production as Afeni Shakur. AllHipHop reported that the casting placed the Oscar-nominated actress opposite Camron Jones’ Tupac while production continued in Southern California.

Snoop Dogg is producing the movie with Death Row Pictures president Sara Ramaker and Imagine Entertainment’s Brian Grazer and Allan Mandelbaum. Universal described the project as the first film under Death Row Pictures’ overall deal with NBCUniversal Entertainment.

The new casting puts Master P’s son inside the story of the deal that helped reshape both men’s legacies. Miller will enter the movie at the point where Snoop’s West Coast career met No Limit’s Southern business machine.

item.title: Megan Thee Stallion Sends Thin Ice Into Hot 100 At No. 68
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Megan Thee Stallion lands a No. 68 Hot 100 debut with Thin Ice as her Tina Tuesday freestyle gains national chart momentum.
item.content:encoded:
Megan Thee Stallion has pushed “Thin Ice” onto the Billboard Hot 100, giving her Tina Tuesday freestyle series a new national chart result.

Billboard’s chart history for Megan lists the song at No. 68 for the week dated November 7, 2026. The entry is also marked as its peak and first week on the chart.

The Hot 100 combines streaming activity, radio audience and sales data, giving the debut a broader measure than any single platform’s play count.

The placement extends a run that began with a stripped-down video rather than a traditional single campaign. Megan released the official “Thin Ice” performance on her YouTube channel October 20, placing herself in an empty industrial space with a direct-to-camera performance and no guest artist.

The song later moved to streaming platforms as part of her Tina Tuesday rollout. By October 29, AllHipHop reported that its daily U.S. on-demand streams had climbed 152 percent across a three-day stretch, rising from 98,000 to 247,000. At that point, the track had not yet entered the Hot 100.

Its No. 68 debut changes that picture. “Thin Ice” now has a measurable chart foothold after moving from a freestyle video to streaming services and then onto Billboard’s all-genre ranking.

The record is built around a sample from Limp Bizkit’s “Break Stuff,” but Megan keeps the focus on her own voice.

The short runtime and sparse visual presentation leave little room for distractions, making the performance feel closer to a cypher than a full-scale music-video production.

That approach has become part of Megan’s current strategy. Tina Tuesday gives her a recurring lane for fast, self-contained releases while she continues building toward her next larger project. She has kept the series active without treating each installment like a formal album single.

The chart appearance arrives after a busy stretch outside the studio. Megan closed the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show, expanded her Gymshark partnership and challenged Instagram after an AI label appeared on her CFDA Awards photos. “Thin Ice” keeps the music at the center of that wider activity.

For now, No. 68 is the song’s official Hot 100 peak. Its next chart week will show whether the freestyle can hold its position or turn its early momentum into a longer run.

item.title: Key Vhani Testifies She Feared Death Before Fatal Shooting
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Key Vhani testified in her Stand Your Ground hearing, describing fear for her life as a Miami judge weighs her murder case.
item.content:encoded:
Key Vhani testified that she feared for her life before fatally shooting her manager’s friend, as she asked Judge Lody Jean to dismiss her second-degree murder charge under Florida’s Stand Your Ground law.

“I thought I was going to die. I thought I was going to die,” she testified November 5, according to the Miami Herald.

The Miami rapper, whose legal name is Kevhani Camilla Hicks, said Demitrie Harris pinned her down. She testified that she fired after seeing him pull something black from his pocket. Surveillance footage showed Harris running away as she advanced and continued shooting.

Key Vhani said shock and pain explained why she had not mentioned the pocket movement to detectives. After the shooting, her manager, Nathan Smith, struck her with his car. She suffered three fractured ribs.

The shooting followed a night spent promoting her music in Miami in October 2023. Harris was Smith’s friend; she had not known him before that evening.

“I believed this guy could kill me,” she testified. She said she had never fired her gun before the shooting.

The immunity fight was already underway in September, when the court reviewed surveillance video and competing accounts of the confrontation. Her defense argued that she feared another attack after getting away from the men.

Prosecutors argued that she kept firing as Harris tried to escape. Her own testimony now gave Judge Jean her account of why she reached for the weapon.

Florida law allows deadly force when a person reasonably believes it is necessary to prevent imminent death, great bodily harm or a forcible felony. The law removes the duty to retreat for a person who meets its requirements, including being somewhere they have a right to be and not engaging in criminal activity.

The immunity provision gives the pretrial hearing direct consequences for whether a prosecution can proceed. Once a defendant raises a prima facie self-defense immunity claim at that hearing, the party opposing immunity must overcome it with clear and convincing evidence.

She remained on GPS-monitored house arrest with a 9 P.M. curfew. Lawyers were set to return for arguments on November 10.

item.title: EDP445 Case Sparks Dispute Over Sting Group’s Cooperation With Investigators
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: EDP445's revived criminal case draws competing accounts from prosecutors and Predator Poachers as extradition moves forward.
item.content:encoded:
EDP445‘s criminal case has prompted a dispute over whether the online sting group that confronted him in 2021 cooperated with investigators.

Predator Poachers founder Alex Rosen told News 3 his team supplied chat records and account access. Prosecutors have blamed cooperation problems for complicating their earlier review.

“We gave him (investigator) access to all of the accounts,” Rosen said.

Rosen shared emails showing an investigator’s questions about account changes, deleted messages and conversation dates. The exchange included a message dated May 13, 2021.

The former YouTuber, whose legal name is Bryant Moreland, was arrested in Henderson, Nevada, on November 4. Henderson police said officers took him into custody on a warrant shortly before noon near Green Valley and Pebble.

Moreland was booked into the Clark County Detention Center. He remained there Thursday. He had built an audience of millions on YouTube before the 2021 allegations drove him off major social platforms. Content creator JiDion posted footage of officers taking Moreland into custody outside a dialysis center on Corporate Circle.

California prosecutors filed four felony charges on November 2. The counts include attempting lewd acts upon a child, meeting a minor for lewd purposes, contacting a minor with intent to commit a sexual offense and distributing or showing pornography to a minor.

The allegations concern an April 17, 2021 incident in Bakersfield. Predator Poachers used an online decoy who posed as a 13-year-old girl, then recorded a confrontation with Moreland at an apartment complex.

The district attorney’s office reviewed the matter in 2021 and 2022. It said statements Moreland later made in filmmaker Mike Clum’s documentary, The Sick Mind Of EDP445, led prosecutors and sheriff’s investigators to reopen the case.

That documentary appeared on YouTube in August. Former To Catch A Predator host Chris Hansen interviewed Moreland for the film, which returned the long-running allegations to public view.

“We’re looking very forward to assisting in his prosecution in any way possible,” Rosen said.

Moreland is expected in Las Vegas court Monday, November 9, as the extradition process proceeds. Prosecutors said a California arraignment will be set after he returns to Kern County.

item.title: Ben Crump Joins Javits Frimpong’s Family As Bronx Demands Answers
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Javits Frimpong's family retained Ben Crump as a Bronx rally called for action against bullying following the teen's killing.
item.content:encoded:
Javits Frimpong‘s family hired civil rights attorney Ben Crump to pursue answers about the 15-year-old’s killing as Bronx residents gathered Saturday for an anti-bullying rally and memorial.

Crump’s firm announced that he would work with the family. His team will look at what happened before the shooting and whether others may bear responsibility.

Residents and advocates at Saturday’s rally honored Javits and called for more to stop bullying. They also urged action to keep young people safe from violence. Police continued searching for three masked teenagers. Investigators had not said what led to the shooting. The boys were described as about 16 to 18 years old.

Javits was killed on October 29 while heading to DreamYard Preparatory School. The shooting happened near East 171st Street and Crotona Place in the Bronx’s Claremont neighborhood, a few blocks from the school.

He died at St. Barnabas Hospital.

He had left Ghana to join his father, Thomas Frimpong, in New York a year earlier. October 28 marked the anniversary of his arrival in the United States. He was killed the following morning. His family said he wanted to become a doctor.

His mother, Doris Adu Gyamfi, arrived in New York on Wednesday after receiving a visa to attend her son’s funeral. Mayor Zohran Mamdani had sought President Donald Trump’s help securing the visa following the shooting.

Thomas reported that his son had complained of bullying. He said the principal told him two students had been suspended over an incident involving Javits. Police were investigating whether bullying played a role in the killing.

Police had also sought school records about the alleged bullying. They said the Department of Education first required a subpoena to release that information. The department later said it was working with police and would turn over records under the law.

A fundraiser benefiting Thomas had collected $898,199 from more than 27,000 donations toward a $1.1 million goal by November 5.

The money was intended to help with funeral costs, burial arrangements and unexpected expenses.

Crump said his team “will stand with Javits’ family every step of the way until the people responsible are held accountable and his family has the answers they deserve.”

item.title: Chris Brown & Usher Bring Back Duets After Atlanta Backlash
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Chris Brown and Usher performed together Friday after fans criticized the missing duets at their first Atlanta concert.
item.content:encoded:
Chris Brown and Usher performed together Friday in Atlanta, a night after fans complained that their stadium show had left out the duets.

According to TMZ, they performed “Back to Sleep” and the “It Depends” remix. Their separate platforms reportedly matched earlier staging.

The joint performances answered one of the loudest complaints from Thursday’s opening concert at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Attendees had criticized the wait, shortened sets and the absence of songs featuring both headliners. Some called for refunds after leaving the show disappointed.

Those complaints also fed speculation about friction between the singers. Brown responded on his Instagram Story, warning fans not to believe online chatter, without identifying the specific claim he was challenging.

“The R&B Tour” was built around a shared production.

Since the June opening in Denver, Brown and Usher have moved between their solo catalogs and collaborations across nine acts. “New Flame” has been among the joint selections, while Mario, Eric Bellinger and Tank have served as backing vocalists and performed their own music.

Their partnership has also produced major ticket sales. The first 36 reported concerts brought in $284.7 million and more than 1.5 million tickets through October 3. September alone accounted for $77.4 million from 423,000 tickets at 10 shows. July grossed $98.4 million and August added $91.8 million.

That September run made them the first co-headliners to lead the monthly touring chart, as AllHipHop previously reported. The total through early October had already exceeded the $183.9 million earned by Usher’s previous “Past Present Future” tour.

The long run has required adjustments. In October, dates in Cincinnati, Indianapolis and Columbia, South Carolina, were canceled as organizers cited the health and well-being of the touring party and crew.

Atlanta’s five-show booking set a new single-tour-stop mark for Mercedes-Benz Stadium, exceeding the four concerts Beyonce played there on her 2025 “Cowboy Carter” tour. The additional Atlanta date was announced in August as the wider North American tour expanded.

Friday’s concert had originally been set for November 7 before the venue moved it to November 6. After Friday, three Atlanta dates remained on the announced itinerary: November 8, November 10 and November 11.
